title: Unifying governance and metadata across Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio and Atlan
key_points: Partner integration that syncs metadata both ways: technical assets flow from SageMaker Unified Studio into Atlan, and glossary terms and descriptions written in Atlan flow back.
Setup guide for the AWS side and the Atlan connector.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon SageMaker Catalog, Atlan
authors: Atlan — Karan Singh Thakur, Satabrata Paul, Divij Bhatia, Leonardo Gomez

title: Modernize Apache Spark workflows using Spark Connect on Amazon EMR on Amazon EC2
key_points: Do-it-yourself Spark Connect on EMR on EC2: a bootstrap script starts the server and an ALB adds TLS so a laptop IDE can run code on the cluster.
Superseded by native Spark Connect on EMR on EC2 (September 2026), which removes the bootstrap and load-balancer work.
services: Amazon EMR, Apache Spark Connect, Elastic Load Balancing

title: How Taxbit achieved cost savings and faster processing times using Amazon S3 Tables
key_points: Taxbit replaced a database that could not keep up with crypto pricing data by an S3 Tables lakehouse fed by Lambda API pollers and Kinesis, processed with Glue and EMR, orchestrated by Step Functions and queried in Athena.
Data is partitioned by date and exchange; S3 Tables handles compaction and time travel serves audit needs.
AWS reports 82% lower storage infrastructure cost and about 5x faster processing; the post stays at overview level.
services: Amazon S3 Tables, Apache Iceberg, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, AWS Lambda, AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, AWS Step Functions, Amazon Athena
decision: Operational database vs managed Iceberg tables for high-volume, audit-bound time-series data
authors: Taxbit — Larry Christensen, Derek Ziehl, Pranjal Gururani, Washim Nawaz

title: Create and update Apache Iceberg tables with partitions in the AWS Glue Data Catalog using the AWS SDK and AWS CloudFormation
key_points: The Glue CreateTable and UpdateTable APIs, and CloudFormation, can now define Iceberg tables with partition specs, sort order and schema changes.
Before, IaC could only create unpartitioned Iceberg tables and partitions had to be added from an engine like Athena, outside the CI/CD pipeline.
Gives CLI, boto3 and CloudFormation samples.
services: AWS Glue Data Catalog, Apache Iceberg, AWS CloudFormation, AWS SDK for Python (Boto3)
decision: Iceberg table DDL in infrastructure as code vs engine SQL (Athena/Spark) for table lifecycle

title: Power data ingestion into Splunk using Amazon Data Firehose
key_points: Refresh of a 2017 walkthrough: Firehose pushes VPC Flow Logs and CloudWatch logs to Splunk's HTTP Event Collector, with failed records backed up to S3.
Contrasts this push model with Splunk's pull-based add-on that needs pollers on EC2.
services: Amazon Data Firehose, Amazon Kinesis, Amazon CloudWatch, Splunk
authors: Tarik Makota, Mitali Sheth, Roy Arsan, Yashika Jain

title: IPv6 addressing with Amazon Redshift
key_points: Redshift Serverless workgroups can run in dual-stack mode so clients connect over IPv4 or IPv6.
Steps: give the VPC and subnets IPv6 ranges, then switch an existing workgroup (console or CLI) or create a new one dual-stack.
Dual-stack works only with private access for now, not public endpoints.
decision: IPv4-only vs dual-stack networking for a Redshift Serverless workgroup
authors: Srini Ponnada, Zirui Hua, Niranjan Kulkarni, Sandeep Adwankar, Sumanth Punyamurthula, Yanzhu Ji

title: Best practices for querying Apache Iceberg data with Amazon Redshift
key_points: Seven practices for Redshift reading Iceberg: tight data types, partitions on the most-filtered columns at a sensible grain, no SELECT *, and Glue column statistics so the optimizer plans joins well.
Table upkeep (compaction, snapshot expiry, orphan-file removal) is automatic on S3 Tables but must be scheduled with Athena OPTIMIZE/VACUUM or Spark procedures on self-managed tables.
For dashboards, incremental materialized views in Redshift over Iceberg; for shared logic, late-binding views.
services: Amazon Redshift, Apache Iceberg, Amazon S3 Tables, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon Athena
decision: Self-managed Iceberg with scheduled maintenance vs S3 Tables, and which partition grain, for Redshift-queried lake data
attaches_to: aws-bytes: File Layout Optimization (active); dbt-pipelines (Athena + Iceberg folder)
authors: Anusha Challa, Jonathan Katz, Mohammed Alkateb

title: Reference guide for building a self-service analytics solution with Amazon SageMaker
key_points: Retail example where three business units keep data in S3, Redshift and Snowflake across separate accounts; SageMaker Unified Studio federates all three into one catalog without copying.
Adds a business glossary and access rules so analysts can find and query the joined data themselves.
Mostly console steps, including cross-account networking to reach Redshift.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon SageMaker Catalog, Amazon Redshift, Amazon S3, Snowflake, AWS Lake Formation
decision: Copy data into one warehouse vs federate sources into a shared catalog for self-service analytics
authors: Navnit Shukla, Ayan Majumder, Karan Edikala

title: Introducing the Apache Spark troubleshooting agent for Amazon EMR and AWS Glue
key_points: A managed, read-only MCP server reads Spark History Server data, executor logs and configs for a failed Glue or EMR job and returns a root cause and suggested fix in plain language.
Three ways to use it: ask from Kiro CLI, have an Airflow failure callback or an EventBridge rule plus Lambda post the diagnosis to Slack, or chart account-wide failures in an IDE.
Access is limited by IAM and every tool call lands in CloudTrail, which matters for production use.
services: AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, Amazon EventBridge, AWS Lambda, Apache Airflow, Model Context Protocol, Kiro
decision: Plain failure alert vs alert enriched with an agent's root-cause diagnosis for Spark ETL jobs
authors: Jake Zych, Andrew Kim, Maheedhar Reddy Chappidi, Arunav Gupta, Jeremy Samuel, Muhammad Ali Gulzar, Mohit Saxena, Mukul Prasad, Kartik Panjabi, Shubham Mehta, Vishal Kajjam, Vidyashankar Sivakumar, Wei Tang

title: Introducing Apache Spark upgrade agent for Amazon EMR
key_points: An AWS-hosted MCP agent, driven from an IDE such as Kiro, plans a Spark version upgrade, updates build dependencies, rewrites code, runs the job on EMR and compares old and new outputs before handing over a summary.
Comes with a small script that scans EMR steps and charts which heavily used apps sit on versions nearing end of support.
This launch covered EMR; Glue job upgrades with the same approach arrived in a later 2026 post.
services: Amazon EMR, Apache Spark, Kiro, Model Context Protocol
decision: Manual vs agent-assisted Spark version upgrades, and which apps to upgrade first
authors: Keerthi Chadalavada, McCall Peltier, Rajendra Gujja, Bo Li, Malinda Malwala, Mohit Saxena, Mukul Prasad, Vaibhav Naik, Pradeep Patel, Shubham Mehta, XiaoRun Yu

title: How Socure achieved 50% cost reduction by migrating from self-managed Spark to Amazon EMR Serverless
key_points: Socure moved a Kinesis-fed Spark streaming pipeline (raw then processed Delta tables, with field-level encryption) from open-source Spark on EKS to EMR Serverless.
Fewer but larger executors stopped out-of-memory failures, and serverless scaling cut weekend spend.
AWS reports average latency fell by roughly half and total cost by 45-57%, and that EMR Serverless stayed cheaper even after allowing for a Graviton move on EKS.
services: Amazon EMR Serverless, Amazon EKS, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Delta Lake, AWS Graviton
decision: Self-managed Spark on EKS vs EMR Serverless for a variable-load streaming pipeline
authors: Socure — Junaid Effendi, Pengyu Wang, Raj Ramasubbu

title: Amazon EMR HBase on Amazon S3 transitioning to EMR S3A with comparable EMRFS performance
key_points: From EMR 7.10, HBase on S3 writes and reads its data files through EMR S3A instead of EMRFS, while write-ahead logs stay on cluster storage.
Claims performance on par with EMRFS plus the usual benefits of the community connector and SDK v2.
services: Amazon EMR, Apache HBase, Amazon S3
authors: Dong Li, Giovanni Matteo Fumarola, Ramesh Kandasamy

title: Accelerate Apache Hive read and write on Amazon EMR using enhanced S3A
key_points: Hive on EMR now uses EMR's enhanced S3A connector by default instead of EMRFS, with a zero-rename commit path for writes and Lake Formation support.
AWS reports EMR 7.10 Hive reads about 1.5x faster than EMR 7.0 on a 3 TB TPC-DS-derived test, and writes up to 3x faster; notes limits of the zero-rename feature.
services: Amazon EMR, Apache Hive, Amazon S3
authors: Ramesh Kandasamy, Giovanni Matteo Fumarola, Himanshu Mishra, Paramvir Singh, Anmol Sundaram

title: How Bayer transforms Pharma R&D with a cloud-based data science ecosystem using Amazon SageMaker
key_points: Bayer built a pharma R&D data science platform on SageMaker Unified Studio and Catalog, with research domains run as data-mesh products over an S3/Iceberg and Redshift lakehouse.
High-level customer story about tooling choices and planned scale, with no build detail.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon SageMaker Catalog, Amazon SageMaker Lakehouse, Apache Iceberg, Amazon Redshift
authors: Bayer — Avinash Erupaka, Radhika Kashyap, Modood Alvi

title: Introducing Apache Iceberg materialized views in AWS Glue Data Catalog
key_points: The Glue Data Catalog can now own materialized views over Iceberg tables: defined in Spark SQL, stored as Iceberg in S3 or S3 Tables, and refreshed incrementally on a schedule on managed compute.
Spark in Athena, EMR and Glue can silently rewrite matching queries to read the view instead of the base tables.
Works only in AWS's Spark runtime and views are eventually consistent; later 2026 posts cover the feature in more depth.
services: AWS Glue Data Catalog, AWS Glue, Apache Iceberg, Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon EMR, Amazon Athena
decision: Hand-built incremental Glue jobs vs catalog-managed Iceberg materialized views for aggregate layers
authors: Tomohiro Tanaka, Layth Yassin, Leon Lin, Mahesh Mishra, Noritaka Sekiyama

title: Introducing AWS Glue 5.1 for Apache Spark
key_points: Glue 5.1 moved to Spark 3.5.6 and Python 3.11, added Iceberg materialized views and Iceberg format v3, allowed Lake Formation-governed writes, and made S3A the default S3 connector.
Superseded by Glue 6.0 (August 2026) and automatic job version upgrades, so the reader would go straight to the newer runtime.
services: AWS Glue, Apache Spark, Apache Iceberg, AWS Lake Formation
authors: Chiho Sugimoto, Bo Li, Kartik Panjabi, Peter Manastyrny, Noritaka Sekiyama, Peter Tsai

title: SAP data ingestion and replication with AWS Glue zero-ETL
key_points: Glue zero-ETL can replicate SAP objects over OData into S3 Tables, the SageMaker lakehouse or Redshift, with no pipeline code.
Explains three change-capture modes: SAP's own delta queue (catches deletes), a last-modified watermark with upserts (misses physical deletes), and a full reload with upserts as the fallback.
Shows how to read the CloudWatch events and target-side status tables to debug failed or partial syncs.
services: AWS Glue, AWS Glue zero-ETL, Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon Redshift, Amazon CloudWatch, AWS Secrets Manager
decision: Source delta queue vs timestamp watermark vs full reload with upsert for incremental ERP replication
authors: Shashank Sharma, Abhijeet Jangam, Diego Lombardini, Parth Panchal

title: Build billion-scale vector databases in under an hour with GPU acceleration on Amazon OpenSearch Service
key_points: OpenSearch can borrow serverless GPUs while building vector indexes, so very large HNSW indexes are built much faster without running GPU instances full time.
AWS reports indexing up to 10x faster at about a quarter of the cost; an August 2026 post revisits the same feature in more depth.
authors: Dylan Tong, Aruna Govindaraju, Corey Nolet, Kshitiz Gupta, Navneet Verma, Vamshi Vijay Nakkirtha

title: Auto-optimize your Amazon OpenSearch Service vector database
key_points: OpenSearch can now test vector index settings (HNSW parameters, compression, engine) for the reader's own data and suggest configurations that balance recall, latency and memory cost.
Replaces weeks of expert trial-and-error with a managed job run from the vector ingestion page.
authors: Dylan Tong, Huibin Shen, Janelle Arita, Vamshi Vijay Nakkirtha, Vikash Tiwari
